idiom_name: tagged node structs with a fixed children array
implementation_notes: C has no classes or reflection, so the pattern is hand-built: one struct per node kind plus a tag enum, with node-specific payload in ordinary members and the normalized child list as an array of node pointers embedded in every node struct. Embedding a common base struct as the first member (and casting a node pointer to the base) gives the generic walker its uniform child access without duplicating the array, which is the C equivalent of deriving from a common base. Keep the tag next to the child list, not inside the payload union, and prefer a length-checked accessor over direct array indexing when nodes are built by hand.
pitfalls: The base struct must be the first member of every node struct; a cast to struct Node * of a node whose base sits elsewhere (or which embeds it twice) is undefined behaviour and corrupts the child walk.
Fixed-size child arrays cap arity: an unbounded repetition needs a list node or a grown array, and forgetting to update nkids after appending hides the new subtree from every pass.
Nodes are heap-allocated and the walker recurses, so deep trees exhaust the C stack, and freeing the tree requires the same recursion (or an explicit worklist).
